title: Probabilistic FP8 safety limiter and selection tuning for Hopper E4M3/E5M2
creator: Ava Patel
description: Enable a conservative, probabilistic FP8 activation path for Hopper GPUs that biases selection toward E4M3/E5M2 profiles only when statistical safety thresholds are met. This ticket implements a lightweight safety limiter (a stochastic gating layer + micro-binning of per-layer scaling stats) that sits between the calibration service and runtime selector. Goals: (1) reduce incidence of rare numerical regressions on tail workloads, (2) provide fast, observable rollback triggers and (3) make the selector robust to model and input drift without blocking day-to-day rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: FP8 selector returns E4M3/E5M2 for >=95% of stable workloads while keeping per-token latency within target SLOs
Micro-binning telemetry shows <0.1% outlier rate (numeric overflow/nan) across 10M requests in shadow sampling
Automated canary A/B comparing control (INT8) vs FP8 with limiter shows no regression in top-3 QA prompt set (within predefined quality delta)
Rollback can be executed within 2 minutes via runtime flag and triggers an alert in PagerDuty if rollback reason is numeric instability
Change passes security review for new telemetry collection (no PII), and PRs have 2 code reviewers and one numerical stability reviewer
test_plan: Unit tests for stochastic gating logic and micro-bin update atomics
Integration test: replay historical calibration corpus through selector (golden-seed suite) and verify decisions are deterministic-for-seed
Stress test: run mixed workload with long-context chat, high prefix caching and KV-cache eviction to surface drift-induced numeric anomalies
Fuzz/bitflip simulation to validate failsafe branches fire and produce readable diagnostic traces
Shadow canary: 1% of production traffic sampled to runtime shadow path for 72 hours with telemetry retained for 30 days
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dev deploy on small Hopper pool with synthetic traffic (QA); validate micro-bins and gating metrics
Stage 1: dark launch on 0.1% production via shadow path, no traffic served; collect telemetry and golden-seed agreement metrics
Stage 2: canary at 2% traffic with conservative gate thresholds and automated rollback script enabled
Stage 3: gradual ramp to 25% controlled by confidence score; monitor drift and error budget
Stage 4: full rollout if 24h canary shows stable numeric fingerprint and no quality regressions
telemetry_and_slas: Expose micro-bin histograms per layer: scale, zero-point, max-abs, overflow-count
Numeric fingerprint drift detector: cosine similarity between recent and baseline activation distributions
Alert levels: P0 alert for overflow rate >0.01% sustained over 5m; P1 for drift score drop >0.05 in 1h
Cost telemetry to evaluate token-unit savings vs control (INT8) on canary workloads
Retention: 30d for micro-bin aggregates, 90d for golden-seed comparison artifacts
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback if overflow/nan rate exceeds 0.01% over a 5-minute window
Rollback if top-3 QA prompt set quality delta exceeds threshold for two consecutive hourly checks
Manual rollback if telemetry pipeline backfills reveal non-deterministic selector flips affecting production keys
Fallback to INT8 profiles automatically if selector service becomes unavailable
notes: This approach aims to be complementary to existing deterministic calibration pipelines; the limiter adds a probabilistic 'confidence tax' to the selector decisions to reduce rare regressions.
We intentionally avoid large model-driven thresholds; instead use per-shard micro-bins aggregated with exponential decay to adapt to workload shift.
Plan includes a small compute tax on selector (approx +2-4% CPU) — accounted for in cost analysis. If unacceptable, we will move gating to a compiled runtime primitive.
Security reviewed telemetry fields to ensure no user content is indexed; only activation stats (aggregates) are collected
